questions.question: Define a development and explain why packaging is made from one, describing what is seen when a cereal box is opened flat.
questions.expected_answer: A development, or net, is the flat 2D pattern of all the faces of a 3D container drawn at true size side by side and joined along the edges that will be folded, so the container can be cut from sheet material in one piece, creased and assembled. Packaging is made from sheet material (board, plastic sheet, thin metal), and the only way to make a hollow shape from a sheet is to cut a flat pattern and fold it. A slit-open cereal box lies flat as one piece: four side panels in a row, top and bottom flaps attached above and below, and a narrow glue tab along one vertical edge where the seam was; every crease was a fold and every other edge a cut.

questions.question: Describe how to draw the development of a rectangular box 80 mm long, 40 mm wide and 120 mm high, including the line conventions and the two checks.
questions.expected_answer: Draw the four sides in a row in the order they wrap around the box: 80 by 120, 40 by 120, 80 by 120, 40 by 120, sharing vertical edges that will be folds, using feint construction lines and projecting the common 120 mm height. Attach the 80 by 40 top panel to the upper edge of an 80 mm side and the 80 by 40 bottom panel to the lower edge of an 80 mm side. Draw the outer cut edge as a dark continuous outline, fold lines as dashed or thin chain lines, and dimension in millimetres with the scale stated and the overall flat size given. Check that every face appears exactly once at true size and that any two faces sharing a fold line on the paper are neighbours on the box.

questions.question: Explain the purpose of glue tabs, flaps and dust flaps on a development, how they are drawn, and give the developments of a tray and a cylinder.
questions.expected_answer: A glue tab is a strip 10 to 15 mm wide on the free edge of the last side panel, tucked inside and glued to the first panel to close the tube. Top and bottom closures are glue flaps, tuck-in lids with a tongue and slot, or crash-lock bases; dust flaps at the sides of a lid keep contents clean and support the tuck. They are drawn attached along the correct edge with their own dashed fold line, labelled, with corners cut at an angle so they do not snag when folding. A tray is a base with four sides attached along its edges, each side with tabs at its ends that fold round and glue to the next side. A cylinder is a rectangle whose length equals the circumference (pi times diameter) for the curved surface, plus two circles for the ends, with a glue tab beyond the true circumference for the seam.
